paragraphs: Hove Architects Co., Ltd. is a Bangkok-based design studio driven by responsiveness, deep understanding, and thoughtful consideration of each client's unique needs. We craft distinctive designs that balance character, sustainability, and optimization through innovative design technologies.
Founded by a team of passionate young architects, we bring diverse experience across a wide range of projects — from intimate residences to complex public buildings.

Our practice is guided by a commitment to environmental responsibility, cutting-edge computational design, and the fulfillment of client aspirations. We explore multiple alternative ideas to create unexpected connections between practical solutions and conceptual imagination.
At Hove Architects, we are dedicated to shaping design that contributes meaningfully to social, environmental, and business transformation.

projects.title: VC House
paras: The project is a private 5 story residence with a usable area of 980 square meters, built on a limited land plot. The owner's objective was to maximize the building footprint within the legal constraints, while still integrating green spaces into every functional area. A vertical garden is introduced at the heart of the house, seamlessly connecting all floors and allowing natural ventilation to flow throughout the entire residence.

projects.title: BWG95 House
paras: This large private residence, located at the entrance of Soi Bang Waek 95 in Bangkok, offers approximately 1,300 square meters of usable space and accommodates three families within a single complex.
The design concept focuses on fostering interaction among all family members while simultaneously respecting each individual's need for privacy.

Large fin walls and  wooden LOUVER wrap around the building, serving multiple purposes: they provide extensive shading to reduce direct sunlight exposure, create a dynamic and responsive facade, and ensure a high level of privacy for the residents.

projects.title: LND 01 House
paras: LND01 and LND02 are two small private residences, each with a usable area of approximately 170–180 square meters, located in Laonadi Subdistrict, Khon Kaen Province. Both houses share the same plot of land and are connected through a central green space.

The orientation of the buildings is carefully arranged to face toward the central courtyard as much as possible, while still maintaining a high degree of privacy. A front-facing layer of perforated brick walls and large wooden panels serves as a buffer, shielding the interiors from the glare of vehicle headlights coming from within the property.
Behind the wooden façade lies an expansive, double-height living area, designed to provide a sense of spaciousness and comfort, while promoting natural ventilation throughout the house.

projects.title: LND 02 House
paras: LND02 is a compact two-story residence situated on the same plot as LND01, in Laonadi Subdistrict, Khon Kaen Province, Thailand.

Designed with a focus on spatial quality and privacy, the house features a soaring double-height living area, framed by a large wooden façade and delicate louvered screens that filter views and light, offering both openness and seclusion.

The second-floor bedroom gracefully extends into the shared central garden, establishing a direct connection with the surrounding greenery. This subtle architectural gesture enhances the living experience, inviting residents to engage with nature and fostering a serene, contemplative atmosphere throughout the home.

projects.title: Gulshan Resident
paras: The Gulshan Resident is a private urban residence designed to respond to the dense, humid context of Dhaka while offering a refined sense of calm, privacy, and openness. The architectural massing features stacked and cantilevered volumes — each expressing distinct functions — with upper floors wrapped in timber screens for shading and privacy. The façade language reflects a balance between solidity and softness, allowing filtered light and controlled transparency while maintaining a warm, contemporary aesthetic.

Internally, the design emphasizes vertical spatial flow through sunken courtyards, elevated terraces, and a suspended swimming pool that visually anchors the house. Each level interlocks spatially, connecting formal and informal zones while maintaining clear separation between private and communal spaces. Natural ventilation, cross breezes, and landscape integration are carefully orchestrated, creating a home that is environmentally responsive and experientially rich — a multi-generational retreat in the heart of the city.

projects.title: Ban Chom Le
paras: Ban Chom Le revolves around creating a wrap-around verandah, or chan, that acts as a thermal buffer for the main living spaces. This intermediate space facilitates natural ventilation, allowing wind to flow smoothly into the house.

The main structure features a high, gabled ceiling designed to let warm air rise and exit through vents at the top. Cooler air is drawn in from below through perforated brick walls and a curved airflow-guiding wall, meticulously shaped based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to maximize natural ventilation from the southwest. The double-skin façade, composed of perforated brickwork, helps exhaust rising warm air at the second-floor level.

The living area, which is most frequently used during the day, is protected by wide verandahs and extended eaves on all sides to shield the space from direct heat gain. On the west side, an additional roof louver extends beyond the eaves, filtering sunlight and creating deep shade. The ground below features grass pavers to further minimize reflected heat back into the house.

The bedroom areas are strategically located in the northeast wing, where nighttime conditions are naturally cooler. The bedroom walls are shielded from harsh afternoon sunlight, minimizing heat accumulation. Ventilated façades in front and back of the house enhance airflow, while the sloped gabled roofs in the bedroom areas direct heat away from the living spaces, ensuring thermal comfort with minimal mechanical cooling.
In addition to promoting natural ventilation, the sloped gabled roof is oriented to the west and south, offering ideal surfaces for solar panel installation.

This project embodies the essence of a true energy-efficient home — one that minimizes energy consumption in all aspects, from error-reduced construction and passive climate control to the careful selection of durable materials and low-maintenance design strategies.
Through this holistic approach, the house delivers comfort for the body, peace of mind, and long-term financial savings.

projects.title: Focus House
paras: FOCUS HOUSE is a two-story residence and tattoo studio designed around the identity and lifestyle of its owners — a young introverted couple working as tattoo artists. Rather than creating a conventional house, the project aims to establish a private sanctuary disconnected from the chaos of the outside world. The architecture is conceived as a “closed house,” using solid walls, layered spatial organization, and internal courtyards to create privacy while carefully controlling views, light, and atmosphere throughout the home.

The core concept of the project is inspired by the relationship between Positive Area and Negative Area found in tattoo art, where black ink and empty space work together to create depth, balance, and emotion on human skin. This idea is translated architecturally through the manipulation of light and shadow, voids and solid masses, as well as carefully framed openings that allow natural light to shift throughout the day. Much like a tattoo gradually revealing its character through contrast, the house uses shadow as a design medium to shape spatial experience and emotional depth.

The interior spaces are designed to seamlessly merge living and creative functions, with the Tattoo Studio and Workshop positioned as the heart of the house. Internal courtyards and layered openings bring natural light, ventilation, and greenery deep into the project while maintaining a calm and introspective atmosphere. The material palette — consisting of textured concrete, glass blocks, warm wood surfaces, and soft natural tones — reflects the raw yet delicate character of tattoo craftsmanship. More than a residence, FOCUS HOUSE becomes an architectural expression of the owners’ personality, creative process, and way of life.

projects.title: BWG Home Office
paras: The BWG Home Office project integrates office and warehouse functions into a single structure while reinterpreting the typical industrial warehouse image.
Located along Bangwaek Road, the building's considerable mass posed a challenge to the design team — how to maintain a light, modern character without overwhelming the surrounding context.
By introducing strong geometric elements and vertical articulation, the façade breaks down the building’s visual bulk, making the overall form appear more refined and approachable.

A combination of white surfaces and warm wooden textures further softens the architecture, evoking the familiar sense of a modern home rather than a utilitarian storage facility. The project seeks to balance functionality with an inviting, human-centered design language that blends seamlessly into its urban surroundings.

projects.title: LIVINN 91 Hotel
paras: LIVINN 91 Hotel is a small boutique hostel featuring six guest rooms, discreetly nestled in the heart of the vibrant Phahurat district. The project involved the transformation of an old commercial building, with a complete overhaul of its façade and interior spaces.
Key architectural interventions included relocating the staircase and opening up a central courtyard to bring natural light deep into the building and enhance cross-ventilation between floors.
The interior design embraces simplicity, with a soft palette of white tones and natural wood accents, creating a warm, calming atmosphere for guests.

projects.title: Life Ladprao Temporary Sales Office
paras: The Life Ladprao Temporary Sales Office was created to serve as a provisional sales space while the main construction site was being prepared for a new building.

One of the project's key challenges was its location — it had to be constructed directly above an active construction traffic route. Therefore, the structure was elevated 5 meters above ground level, allowing construction vehicles to pass through at all times while simultaneously increasing the visibility of the sales office from a distance.

To address budget constraints, the design team repurposed and adapted the existing façade elements from the previous sales office, giving the new structure a fresh yet cost-effective identity that remained aligned with the project’s branding.

projects.title: Brixton Campus Bangsaen Sales Office
paras: The sales office for Brixton Campus Bangsaen is located near Burapha University in Chonburi Province.
Inspired by the natural forms of coastal waves and the subtle color transitions from sandy beaches to the edge of the sea, the building’s flowing curves introduce a sense of playfulness and energy.

The curvilinear façade design not only evokes the spirit of the seaside but also creates a dynamic and youthful atmosphere, perfectly aligned with the project’s target audience — university students seeking a vibrant living environment.

projects.title: Brixton Campus Bangsaen
paras: Brixton Campus Bangsaen is an eight-story condominium project comprising 246 residential units, developed by Origin Property Public Company Limited as an extension of the Brixton Campus Bangsaen Sales Office.

Drawing inspiration from the natural rhythm of coastal waves and the delicate color transitions from sandy beaches to the sea, the building’s flowing curves bring a sense of excitement and vibrancy to the architectural form.

The development features a range of amenities, including a lobby on the ground floor, a fitness center on the seventh floor, and a rooftop swimming pool on the eighth floor, offering residents a dynamic and relaxing lifestyle connected to the spirit of the coastal environment.

projects.title: Viranya Kingkaew Clubhouse
paras: The clubhouse for the Viranya Bangna–Suvarnabhumi project is a 250-square-meter facility designed in a modern farmhouse style.

The program includes a welcoming lobby, a fitness room, a salt-based sauna, and a half-Olympic swimming pool. The architectural inspiration draws from the traditional Western farmhouse typology, simplified through the use of geometric forms to create a design that is both modern and elegant.
With a restrained material palette and clean lines, the clubhouse embodies sophistication without unnecessary ornamentation, a peaceful yet sophisticated environment

projects.title: Bangkok Boulevard Signature Sathorn Pinklao
paras: The clubhouse design for Bangkok Boulevard Signature Sathorn Pinklao draws inspiration from the architectural elements of the renowned Musée d'Orsay in France.

The building features a reinterpretation of the classic Mansard roof, adapted into an asymmetrical form to create a more modern and dynamic aesthetic. A sequence of colonnaded pillars enhances the verticality and grandeur of the structure, while the rhythmic repetition of geometric elements evokes the feeling of curated frames within a museum setting.
This architectural language extends seamlessly into the grand entrance gateway, unifying the entire development under a concept of timeless elegance and artistic influence.

projects.title: Bangkok Boulevard Signature Ramintra-Prayasuren
paras: The clubhouse at Bangkok Boulevard Signature Ramintra-Prayasuren features a distinctive white architecture, defined by flowing walls that elegantly divide the spaces.

Inspired by the Barroco Museum, known for its pure white forms and organic curves symbolizing water emerging from the earth, the design captures this essence by surrounding spaces with gentle, undulating walls.

The centerpiece is a 20-meter swimming pool, partially embraced by the building’s curving forms. The sweeping white walls soften the building’s mass, create shading to reduce heat gain, and seamlessly blend indoor and outdoor spaces. Large elliptical openings carved into the walls create a dramatic sense of arrival, promote natural ventilation, and visually connect the garden with the interior spaces.

The 45-degree placement of the pool further enhances spatial dynamics — one end tucked into the clubhouse for added privacy, while the other extends outward, offering a stunning approach and a swimming experience immersed in lush greenery.

The layout draws inspiration from the concept of a museum, where every space is designed to spark inspiration. Special focal points — such as sculptural trees embraced by oval staircases — serve as visual anchors, offering moments of calm discovery throughout the complex.

projects.title: Bangkok Boulevard Bangna KM.12
paras: The architecture is defined by a single dominant form: the elliptical shape, layered and rotated at varying angles to create an engaging, organic form. The massing evokes a sculptural quality, as if the structure is blooming from the earth.
Signature patterns found on feature walls and signage are derived from the intricate textures of Desert Rose petals, reinforcing the natural, flowing aesthetic of the overall composition.

At the heart of the layout, a courtyard swimming pool provides privacy for users while enhancing natural ventilation throughout the building. The surrounding architecture offers shading, ensuring that the pool area remains usable and comfortable throughout the day.
The circulation design distinctly separates public and private users:
The main entrance is reserved for external visitors.
The secondary entrance provides direct, secure access for residents.
A Customer Service (C.S.) room is also strategically positioned to assist residents with project-related needs, enhancing both convenience and privacy.

projects.title: Matter Ngamwongwan
paras: Matter Ngamwongwan, developed by SC Asset Corporation, is a new-generation townhouse project that reflects the spirit of modern individuals — bold in self-expression yet respectful of context. The design highlights playful arch forms to convey softness and individuality, while maintaining a refined atmosphere through muted, elegant color tones. The overall composition achieves a balance between confident distinctiveness and understated sophistication.

projects.title: Lotus Multipurpose Pavilion
paras: The Multipurpose Pavilion project at Wat Na Luang, Udon Thani Province, is inspired by the Buddhist teaching "A Blooming Lotus at the Center of the Mind," with the lotus symbolizing wisdom, growth, and liberation. The architectural design expresses this concept through the forms of blooming lotus flowers, floating lotus leaves, and rising stems reaching toward the light. The project thoughtfully integrates functional spaces, natural ventilation, and refined decorative details to create an environment that fosters Vipassana meditation, mindfulness, and genuine spiritual development.

projects.title: BE’ON Kaset-Nawamin
paras: The BE’ON Kaset–Nawamin project communicates the brand’s identity through the concept of “Art of Reflection” — an architectural interpretation of how space can mirror the lifestyle, warmth, and individuality of its residents. The clubhouse embraces a series of flowing curves, warm materials, and transparency. Brass tones, timber textures, and large glass panels work together to create a space that feels calm, refined, and welcoming. This design philosophy reflects the idea that architecture is not just a backdrop, but a reflection of the people who live within it.

The spatial composition of the clubhouse and entrance gate illustrates a deep understanding of modern life’s rhythm. Repetitive vertical elements, elevated volumes, and curved rooflines provide a sense of movement, balance, and continuity. More than just aesthetics, every moment of interaction — walking through, passing by, pausing to rest — is crafted to feel intentional and meaningful. The result is a space that not only serves functional needs but also creates an emotional connection between people and place.

projects.title: Ruamjaidhamma Monastery
paras: TThis concept draws inspiration from Mo Hin Khao, often referred to as Thailand’s Stonehenge, a natural rock formation shaped over millions of years through sedimentation and erosion. The design reflects the values of time, stillness, and the quiet power of nature. Architectural forms are intentionally reduced to simple, solid masses, expressing clarity and permanence, much like stone pillars standing within a natural landscape. Emphasis is placed on mass, proportion, and carefully composed openings to create meaningful light and shadow.

The design further integrates principles derived from Suan Mokkh philosophy and traditional Thai architectural “recessed geometry,” fostering an atmosphere of calm, simplicity, and contemplative use. Architectural elements are stripped of excess ornamentation, focusing instead on balance between space, light, and the surrounding environment. The result is a contemporary architectural expression that respects cultural roots and natural context, delivering a refined, restrained, and enduring identity.

projects.title: Cultural Center of Norwegian Waterfront
paras: This cultural center design takes inspiration from the natural form of the Norwegian fjords, transforming the building into a landform that feels carved by nature rather than constructed. The sloping mass, terraced roof, and sunken interior spaces mimic the dramatic topography of glacial valleys, allowing the architecture to blend into the waterfront while still maintaining a powerful visual presence. Rather than placing a standalone object on the site, the building invites people to walk over it, around it, and through it, echoing the way fjords are explored — gradually, and with shifting perspectives.

The project also responds to its urban context by creating a seamless connection between city and sea. Public spaces extend across the roof and landscape, offering a continuous pedestrian experience that connects Oslo’s urban grid with its harbor. The material palette, likely referencing wood and natural tones, strengthens the building’s relationship to nature while maintaining a contemporary Scandinavian character. Ultimately, this proposal is not just a cultural venue — it is a spatial interpretation of Norway’s landscape identity.

projects.title: Banpu Cooling District Plant
paras: BANPU COOLING DISTRICT PLANT reimagines architecture as a living interface between people and the environment. The concept centers around creating a Public Realization Area — a space that not only supports daily functions, but also embodies the company’s Green Concept through direct experience. By maximizing usable space at ground level, integrating light-filled voids, and layering green zones with dust-trapping, oxygen-producing, and air-purifying plants, the project transforms sustainability into something tangible and engaging. Visitors don’t just see “green,” they move through it, breathe it, and understand its value.

A key architectural expression is found in the façade, composed of aluminium composite panels with color and shape gradation inspired by the Banpu logo. This element provides sun shading, airflow, and visual rhythm throughout the day — acting as a functional filter and a brand statement at once. More than just a wrapper, the façade becomes a living skin, reflecting the project’s core vision: sustainability not as an add-on, but as a natural extension of space, technology, and identity.

projects.title: PVR Spa
paras: Nestled along the Vez River in northern Portugal, where the landscape transforms gently with the seasons, the project is conceived in close dialogue with its natural surroundings. Architectural masses are layered, rotated, and spaced with intention to frame the most compelling views toward the river and the distant mountains. Rather than merely organizing functions, the composition choreographs a rhythm of light, shadow, and openness that shifts gracefully throughout the day.

The design embraces the principles of light therapy as a core strategy. Natural light serves not only as an atmospheric feature but as a restorative force, scientifically proven to regulate hormonal balance, reduce stress, and enhance overall well-being. In this way, light becomes an integral part of the architecture: quiet yet powerful, fostering healing, equilibrium, and a deeper connection between people and place.
